title: Pruning preserves execution outside a path
statement: Let $X$, $Y$, and $\alpha$ be types, and let $s$ and $p$ be deterministic two-party communication protocols with inputs in $X$ and $Y$ and outputs in $\alpha$. Suppose a specified subprotocol path witnesses that $s$ lies below $p$, and that $s$ has strictly fewer leaves than $p$. For any inputs $x\in X$ and $y\in Y$ such that either Alice's input or Bob's input is inconsistent with the corresponding branching choices along this path, pruning the path from $p$ returns the same output on $(x,y)$ as $p$.
hypotheses_covered: $s$ and $p$ are protocols over inputs $X,Y$ and outputs in $\alpha$
A specified subprotocol path from $s$ to $p$
At least one of $x$ or $y$ is inconsistent with the corresponding choices along the path
replaced:
Let $p$ be a deterministic two-party communication protocol with Alice inputs in $X$ and
Bob inputs in $Y$, and let $s$ be a rooted subprotocol of $p$, witnessed by a
subprotocol path from the root of $p$ down to the root of $s$. Suppose $s$ has strictly
fewer leaves than $p$, so that pruning this path yields a protocol $p'$. Then for every
input pair $(x,y)$ that does not reach $s$ along this path — that is, $x$ is not among
the Alice inputs consistent with all of Alice's branching choices on the path, or $y$ is
not among the Bob inputs consistent with all of Bob's choices on it — the pruned
protocol $p'$ and the original protocol $p$ return the same value on $(x,y)$.
